# EBMC differential contract (opt-in)

These tests compare the **hand-derived trace tables** of this repository (`tests/functional_tests/reference_semantics/fixtures/*.trace`) with an independent implementation: EBMC 6.1, with Spot's `ltl2tgba` (2.16.1) for EBMC's Büchi route. Both read the same IEEE 1800-2017 text; where they agree on a case, the table has a second, independent confirmation, and where they disagree, a person derives the answer from the standard by hand. Nothing is taken from EBMC as ground truth (`../CONTRACT.md` 5), and EBMC is not a timing oracle: **only trace validity is compared, never failure times**.

The tools are EBMC (`SVA2YOSYS_EBMC`, a command, e.g. through WSL; `--external-tools=ebmc`) and Spot (`SVA2YOSYS_LTL2TGBA`, the directory that contains `ltl2tgba`; `--external-tools=spot`). Spot is GPL-3.0 and is only run as an external program, never linked or shipped; it reaches EBMC through the `PATH` of EBMC's process alone. No corpus is needed: the inputs are this repository's own trace files, so the shared rules of the external areas (`../CONTRACT.md`) apply with the digest taken over those files. The mechanics (selection, design, command, answers, classes) are the contract of `tests/support/ebmc_differential.py` and are tested in `tests/unit_tests/test_ebmc_differential.py`.

## What is compared

1. **Only what the allow-list admits.** `fixtures/allow_list.txt` is the only way into the comparison. Everything else is `not compared`, with a reason: an exclusion (`disable-iff`, `initial-procedure`, `assume-kind` for the fairness assumptions, `x-z-literal`, `cover-vacuity`, `sampled-value-functions` for `$past` and the edge functions, `isunknown`, `system-functions`, `inside`, `goto-nonconsecutive-ranges`, `pending-match-operators` for `intersect`, `within` and `throughout`, `unbounded-under-not`) or `unlisted-shape` (no shape admits the property). The exclusions are the areas where the EBMC feature study found that EBMC reads the standard differently or cannot decide (`docs/tool-comparison.md`); the shapes are the constructs it was calibrated on. A new construct enters by a new shape, never by widening a comparison silently.
2. **Three engines, each for what it decides.** `bmc` (`--bound`) for finite and bounded properties; `bdd` (plain `--bdd`) for the properties that engine accepts on a lasso (`always s_eventually`, `s_eventually`); `buechi` (`--bdd --buechi`, needs Spot) for strong sequences, `s_until`, `s_eventually always` and `s_eventually` (each attempt alone), never for recurrence (`always s_eventually` under Büchi gives false refutations, because EBMC checks Büchi acceptance as the CTL formula `AF AG`). No engine decides fairness assumptions.
3. **Trace validity, not failure times.** For `bmc`, the design replays the written samples and the bound is the number of written samples minus one, so EBMC sees exactly the written samples: an `assert` fails iff the case has a `fail` mark, a `cover` is reached iff it has a `pass` mark. For `bdd` and `buechi`, the design replays the infinite trace (the written samples, then the loop forever): the attempt started at each written sample fails iff its `inf-outcome` is `F` (for `bdd`, the single directive covers every attempt, so it fails iff any is `F`); a disabled attempt is not compared.
4. **One allow-list entry, two controls.** Every shape names a positive control (a case whose expected verdict is a pass, or a cover that is reached) and a negative control (a case whose expected verdict is a failure, or a cover that is not reached), both admitted by that shape (its first shape for the engine) and both recorded `agrees`. The controls run in the default tier: a tool that agrees with everything, or with nothing, fails them.

## Classes (`fixtures/expectations.txt`)

5. **One line per case and engine.** `<trace file stem>:<case> <engine> <class> [detail]`; a case that no engine compares has the engine `-`. The table lists exactly the selections of the allow-list: a case missing from it, a stale case, or another engine fails.
6. **`agrees`.** Every compared label equal. **`disagrees`** is never a recorded class: a disagreement is derived by hand from IEEE 1800 and either becomes a counterexample case with a fix (our table was wrong) or the construct is excluded with the reason (EBMC's reading differs); until then the line is `TODO` and the area fails.
7. **`not compared <reason>`.** Not admitted (point 1), or admitted but EBMC does not decide (`engine-undecided: ...`: a timeout, an unsupported property). **`error <fragment>`.** EBMC fails on the design (a frontend limit); the fragment is part of its message.
8. **The recorded class is checked.** The test runs the case and checks the class and, for `not compared` and `error`, that the detail contains the recorded text; a change in EBMC or in the design that moves a case fails until the line is reviewed.

## Pinning and tiers

9. **The inputs and the tools are the classified ones.** The table records `traces-sha256` (SHA-256 of all the `*.trace` files, line ends normalised to LF, in name order), `ebmc-version` (`6.1 (ebmc-6.1)`) and `spot-version` (`2.16.1`). The digest is checked once per session by a fixture on which every tool test of the area depends (a changed trace file makes them all fail, never skip, with one message to reclassify); one test checks it directly and needs no tool. Every tool comparison depends on session fixtures checking the applicable versions and failing with the instruction to reclassify. EBMC-only runs and individually selected controls check EBMC without requiring Spot; B?chi runs additionally check Spot. A local fake-EBMC regression selects only a BMC control with Spot unselected and requires a version mismatch to stop before the design is run.
10. **Spot reaches EBMC.** With a deliberately failing `ltl2tgba` in the configured directory, the Büchi route fails (`error` or undecided), even when the real Spot directory is already on the inherited PATH; with Spot's configured directory it runs. The configured directory must take precedence over other installations, including Linux search directories under WSL. A probe reads the actual Linux PATH and requires the translated configured directory first; directory names with spaces and shell metacharacters remain literal.
11. **Tiers.** The controls (point 4), the digest and version guards, the mechanism check (point 10) and a check that the comparison can disagree (a control with its expected verdict flipped) run in the **default** tier with `--external-tools=ebmc,spot`. Every case of the table is `slow`, one test per case and engine.
